items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: the first black guitarist that I heard, that really should I say influenced me was Eddie Durham.

ctx.x: No, he mentioned -- it was so -- I liked Frankie Trumbauer so much, myself, and I broached the subject to him because I saw the similarity. Because there was just a plain quality to Frankie Trumbauer's playing that always kind of grabbed me. Something a little different. And I recognized the same thing in Lester's playing. And finally I asked him and he told me that he was influenced by Frankie Trumbauer.

But, as I said, this is to show you how these things go right down the line. So that is where it all began, you know, and I think that they should kind of check back, you know, and -- see, now, as I told you, the first black guitarist that I heard, that really should I say influenced me was Eddie Durham. And he was a trombonist, but a marvelous guitarist, and there was another one and I can't think -- here's another trombonist. His name was Coffee and he played very fine guitar. I'm trying to think whose band he…

But as I say, this -- the kids should really look back and see, you know, go back and listen to what was happening. And on guitar a lot of them are, because a lot of them are listening to Christian, you know. But it didn't -- who was Christian influenced by. See, this is -- someone told me and Led Belly I forgot. Oh, it wasn't Led Belly. I forget who it was, it'll come to me in a moment. But these are the things that I would advise them to do.
